# Discussion

**Main finding.** On Gemma 3 270M, a dual-effect sparse intervention
produces large free-generation article--noun rewrites, but the six-cell
split shows that those rewrites are carried by the generated article.
Inserting `a` versus `an` with the intervention off already moves noun
distributions by TV \(0.937\). For S1 at \(5\times\), treated-article
insertion reproduces the new top-1 noun on 20/20 prompts;
\(\operatorname{cosine}(E_M,E_T)=0.95\), while matched-prefix leftover TV
is \(0.028\). Attribution-selected content-ish features (S3) do not move
nouns. The S1 leftover under `an` is small, already present at
\(1.5\times\), and comparable to a matched random control.

This is a **transmission** result, not a verdict that no latent plan
exists. H1/H2-style claims about what is represented at \(P\) and H3-style
claims about how a later effect is transmitted are not mutually exclusive.
The assay distinguishes generated-token relay from matched-prefix leftover.
It does not distinguish fused packages from modular plans.

**Replay as a falsifier.** Treated-article insertion with the intervention
off is a simple causal-scrubbing test [@chan2022scrubbing]: if the later
noun change is carried by the article token, substituting that token into
an unintervened run should recreate most of the change. It does. The
exact identity \(E_T=E_M+E_R\) makes that statement a vector split rather
than a slogan.

**Closed loop.** In an autoregressive model the generated article is
self-generated feedback. An internal intervention can change later
computation by changing that feedback even if leftover internal control of
the noun is negligible. Measuring both routes is the mechanistic analogue
of separating an organism's internal state from the sensory consequences
of its own action. We do not import a neuroscience literature; we note
the architectural fact that the output is part of the circuit.

**Methodological standard.** For any multi-token causal claim, report the
six cells, print \(E_T=E_M+E_R\) before TV, report leftovers under both
token values, and compare the intervention-off token contrast to the
total effect. Keep the original intervention on in matched-prefix cells,
recompute the full sequence, use target-free distributional distances,
list pre-specified lexical contrasts individually when \(N\) is small,
trace cross-token reachability, and validate sensitivity both with known
mechanisms and with an upstream reference on the studied stack. Without
this split, a later-token change is evidence of coordinated output, not
identified leftover internal control.
